neighbours.label: 'wear' as a verb of things wearing out with use ('tires will wear unevenly', 'the pads wear down'); 'wear' meaning to have clothes on, and the same objects without wear, stay quiet.
fire: Cheap brake pads wear quickly in city traffic.
The hinges will wear if you don't oil them.
Soft tyres wear faster on hot roads.
The steps began to wear after centuries of use.
Misaligned wheels make tyres wear unevenly.
Plastic gears wear down over time.
The carpet will wear thin near the door.
Knife edges wear with daily use.
quiet: Cheap brake pads squeal in city traffic.
Guests should wear a jacket to the dinner.
Soft tyres grip better on hot roads.
The steps were rebuilt after centuries of use.
Children wear uniforms at the school.
Plastic gears are cheap to make.
She will wear a red dress to the party.

notes: Card: ' in' x4, ' True' x2, ' fat' x2, ' wear', ' brakes' (Underinflated tires are under stress and will⟦ wear⟧ unevenly; applies the⟦ brakes⟧). Exploratory probe: 'tires will wear unevenly' 0.55; 'applies the brakes' -0.01; 'tires are a problem' 0.07. Near misses include 'wear' for clothes, to test the meaning.
